note.explanation: A computing system needs hardware, software, and electricity to work. Networks and the Internet are also computing systems that connect devices and help them share information.
examples: A school LAN connects computers and printers within the school.
The Internet connects networks across the world.
note.checkAnswer: A LAN connects computers in a specific area, such as one building or school.
note.simple: Hardware is the equipment, software gives it instructions, and electricity powers it. Networks connect devices so they can communicate and share resources.
note.checkQuestion: What type of network connects computers in a specific area, such as a school?
note.title: Computing Systems
steps: Identify the hardware: the physical devices.
Identify the software: the instructions and programs.
Check that electricity is available to power the hardware.
For a network, identify how devices connect and share information.
note.answer: A computing system uses hardware, software, and electricity to process data and perform tasks.

options: It connects networks worldwide to facilitate communication and data exchange
It connects computers only within one building
It supplies electricity to computer hardware
It is software used only for word processing
mcqs.stem: What is the primary objective of the Internet?
rationales: Correct: the Internet connects networks worldwide and enables communication and data exchange.
Incorrect: this describes a LAN, not the Internet's worldwide reach.
Incorrect: electricity powers hardware; it is not the Internet's objective.
Incorrect: word processing is a function of application software.

options: A physical medium for data transfer
A device that transmits data packets between networks
mcqs.stem: Which item is identified as a physical medium for data transfer in a network?
rationales: Correct: network cables provide a physical medium for data transfer.
Incorrect: this describes a protocol.
Incorrect: this describes a router.
Incorrect: POP is used for retrieving emails.

mcqs.stem: Which type of network connects computers across large geographic regions?
rationales: Incorrect: a LAN connects computers in a specific area, such as a building or school.
Correct: a WAN connects computers across larger geographic regions.
Incorrect: a switch connects devices within a network.
Incorrect: TCP/IP is a set of Internet protocols, not a network type.

mcqs.stem: Which network device transmits data packets between networks?
rationales: Correct: routers transmit data packets between networks.
Incorrect: a network cable is a physical medium for data transfer.
Incorrect: switches connect devices in a network and facilitate communication.
Incorrect: a web browser lets a user request and view web pages.

mcqs.stem: Which protocol is used for retrieving emails from a server or network?
rationales: Incorrect: FTP is used for transferring files between computers.
Incorrect: UDP is described as faster but less reliable.
Correct: POP is used for retrieving emails from a server or network.
Incorrect: TCP/IP governs data transmission over the Internet.

mcqs.stem: Which category includes an operating system that manages a computer's resources?
rationales: Incorrect: application software carries out functions for the user.
Correct: system software includes the operating system and utilities that manage computer resources.
Incorrect: a network cable is hardware, not a software category.
Incorrect: electricity is a power source, not software.

options: A LAN connects a specific area; a WAN connects a larger geographic region
A LAN uses software; a WAN uses hardware
A LAN retrieves email; a WAN transfers files
A LAN is the Internet; a WAN is a web browser
mcqs.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes a LAN from a WAN?
rationales: Correct: a LAN covers a specific area, while a WAN covers larger geographic regions.
Incorrect: both types of networks can use hardware and software.
Incorrect: email retrieval and file transfer are not the definitions of LAN and WAN.
Incorrect: a LAN is not the Internet, and a WAN is not a web browser.

options: The environment influences network design, security, and performance
The environment replaces the need for network software
The environment makes all networks operate identically
The environment is the same thing as a network protocol
mcqs.stem: Why is a network's operating environment important?
rationales: Correct: the environment influences network design, security, and performance.
Incorrect: network software is still needed, including protocols and network operating systems.
Incorrect: networks can operate in different environments, which influence their design and performance.
Incorrect: a protocol is a rule for data exchange, not the network's environment.

written.text: Describe the main components of a computer system.

rubric.why: Hardware is one of the three main components.
rubric.how: Name the tangible components, such as the CPU, RAM, storage, and input/output devices.

rubric.why: Software and electricity complete the three main components.
rubric.how: Name software as instructions for hardware and electricity as its power source.

modelAnswer: Hardware refers to the tangible components of the system, such as the CPU, RAM, storage devices, and input and output devices.
Software is a collection of instructions that dictate the requirements and actions that hardware must do.
Electricity is the power source that enables the hardware components to function.
Therefore, the main components are hardware, software, and electricity.

modelAnswer: The types of computing systems include computers, software systems, computer networks, and the Internet.
A computer is a system designed to process data and perform tasks according to instructions.
Software is a collection of instructions that dictate the requirements and actions that hardware must do.
System software manages computer resources, while application software carries out certain functions for the user.
A computer network connects multiple computers and devices, enabling the exchange of resources and information.
Networks can share files, printers, and Internet access and can enable communication and data management.
The Internet connects multiple networks worldwide, including private, public, academic, business, and government networks.
Its primary objective is to facilitate communication and data exchange between computers and users globally.

examTips: Short questions may ask you to name the three requirements of a computing system, list types of computing systems, or describe computer-system components.
For a list question, include every item asked for: hardware, software, and electricity; or computer, software systems, computer networks, and the Internet.
In long questions, earn marks by naming each type and giving its purpose. Add details such as resource sharing and communication for networks, and worldwide data exchange for the Internet.
Use the textbook's terms: routers transmit data packets between networks, switches connect devices in a network, and network cables provide a physical medium for data transfer.

explain.title: What is a computer system?
explain.body: A computer system is a structured set of hardware and software components specifically designed for data processing and the performance of various operations. Its basic task is to execute programs and manage data to achieve objectives such as problem solving, process control, and communication aid.

explain.title: Three requirements
explain.body: The three basic requisites needed to run a computing system are hardware, software, and electric power. Hardware means the tangible components. Software is a collection of instructions that dictate the requirements and actions that hardware must do. Electricity enables the hardware to function.

explain.title: Networks and their parts
explain.body: A computer network connects multiple computers and devices so they can exchange resources and information. Routers transmit data packets between networks; switches connect devices in a network; cables provide a physical medium for data transfer. Protocols are rules for data exchange.

explain.title: LAN, WAN, and the Internet
explain.body: A LAN connects computers in a specific area, such as a building or school. A WAN connects computers across larger geographic regions. The Internet connects multiple networks worldwide to facilitate communication and data exchange.

mistakes: Do not confuse hardware, software, and electricity: they are different requirements of a computing system.
Do not say that a switch transmits data packets between networks; the section assigns that role to routers.
Do not describe a LAN as worldwide. A LAN covers a specific area; a WAN covers larger geographic regions.
Do not leave out one of the four types when asked to list the types of computing systems.
Do not confuse protocols with hardware: protocols are rules and conventions for data exchange.
